title: TOPIK I
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public TOPIK I syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: You hear the greeting '안녕하세요?' (annyeonghaseyo). Which response is the most natural reply in a TOPIK I listening exchange?
items.explanation: The greeting 안녕하세요 is answered with the same greeting 안녕하세요. The other choices express a request, thanks, or uncertainty and do not fit a greeting exchange.

items.stem: You hear the thanks '감사합니다' (gamsahamnida). Which reply is the most natural in a beginner-level listening exchange?
options: 잘 먹겠습니다 (jal meokgetseumnida) - I will eat well
items.explanation: 감사합니다 'thank you' is naturally answered with 천만에요 'you're welcome'. The others are a greeting, a mealtime phrase, and an apology, none of which reply to thanks.

items.stem: You hear '이름이 뭐예요?' (ireumi mwoyeyo?) asking for a name. Which answer fits the question best?
options: 저는 스무 살이에요 (jeoneun seumu sarieyo) - I am twenty years old
저는 한국 사람이에요 (jeoneun hanguk saramieyo) - I am Korean
제 이름은 민수예요 (je ireumeun Minsuyeyo) - My name is Minsu
저는 학생이에요 (jeoneun haksaengieyo) - I am a student
items.explanation: 이름이 뭐예요? asks 'what is your name?', so the fitting reply gives a name. Age, nationality, and occupation answer different personal-information questions.

items.stem: You hear '어디에 가요?' (eodie gayo?) meaning 'Where are you going?'. Which reply answers it correctly?
options: 세 시예요 (se siyeyo) - It is three o'clock
김치를 좋아해요 (gimchireul joahaeyo) - I like kimchi
네, 좋아요 (ne, joayo) - Yes, that is fine
학교에 가요 (hakgyoe gayo) - I am going to school
items.explanation: 어디에 가요? asks about a destination, so 학교에 가요 answers with a place. Clock time, food preference, and agreement do not answer a 'where' question.

items.stem: You hear '몇 시예요?' (myeot siyeyo?) meaning 'What time is it?'. Which reply is correct?
options: 세 시예요 (se siyeyo) - It is three o'clock
학교에 가요 (hakgyoe gayo) - I go to school
오월 오일이에요 (owol oilieyo) - It is May 5th
네 명이에요 (ne myeongieyo) - There are four people
items.explanation: 몇 시예요? asks the hour, so 세 시예요 gives a time of day. A place, a date, and a number of people answer other kinds of questions.

items.stem: You hear '무슨 음식을 좋아해요?' (museun eumsigeul joahaeyo?) meaning 'What food do you like?'. Which reply fits?
options: 커피를 마셔요 (keopireul masyeoyo) - I drink coffee
김치를 좋아해요 (gimchireul joahaeyo) - I like kimchi
물을 주세요 (mureul juseyo) - Please give me water
밥을 먹어요 (babeul meogeoyo) - I eat rice
items.explanation: The question asks which food one likes, so 김치를 좋아해요 states a liked food. The others describe drinking, requesting, or eating rather than food preference.

items.stem: You hear '생일이 언제예요?' (saengiri eonjeyeyo?) meaning 'When is your birthday?'. Which reply is right?
options: 스무 살이에요 (seumu sarieyo) - I am twenty
세 시예요 (se siyeyo) - It is three o'clock
오월 오일이에요 (owol oilieyo) - It is May 5th
items.explanation: 생일이 언제예요? asks for a date, so 오월 오일이에요 gives the birthday date. Age, clock time, and a weekday answer different 'what/when' questions.

items.stem: You hear '주말에 뭐 해요?' (jumare mwo haeyo?) meaning 'What do you do on weekends?'. Which reply fits?
options: 두 개예요 (du gaeyo) - There are two
주말이 좋아요 (jumari joayo) - I like weekends
친구를 만나요 (chingureul mannayo) - I meet a friend
items.explanation: 주말에 뭐 해요? asks about a weekend activity, so 친구를 만나요 names an activity. A day, a quantity, and a preference do not describe an activity.

items.stem: You hear '커피 마실래요?' (keopi masillaeyo?) meaning 'Would you like to drink coffee?'. Which reply accepts the offer?
options: 네, 좋아요 (ne, joayo) - Yes, that sounds good
네, 학생이에요 (ne, haksaengieyo) - Yes, I am a student
아니요, 커피예요 (aniyo, keopiyeyo) - No, it is coffee
네, 세 시예요 (ne, se siyeyo) - Yes, it is three
items.explanation: The offer 커피 마실래요? is accepted with 네, 좋아요. The other replies attach unrelated information about identity, a noun, or a time to the agreement.

items.stem: You hear '화장실이 어디에 있어요?' (hwajangsiri eodie isseoyo?) meaning 'Where is the restroom?'. Which reply locates it?
options: 화장실이 없어요 (hwajangsiri eopseoyo) - There is no restroom
저기 오른쪽에 있어요 (jeogi oreunjjoge isseoyo) - It is over there on the right
네, 있어요 (ne, isseoyo) - Yes, there is
화장실을 좋아해요 (hwajangsireul joahaeyo) - I like restrooms
items.explanation: 어디에 있어요? asks for a location, so 저기 오른쪽에 있어요 gives a position. Repeating a denial, a yes/no answer, or a preference does not give a location.

items.stem: You hear '이 옷 얼마예요?' (i ot eolmayeyo?) meaning 'How much is this clothing?'. Which reply gives the price?
options: 두 시예요 (du siyeyo) - It is two o'clock
세 개예요 (se gaeyo) - There are three
만 원이에요 (man wonieyo) - It is ten thousand won
옷이 좋아요 (osi joayo) - The clothes are nice
items.explanation: 얼마예요? asks a price, so 만 원이에요 answers with an amount of money. A time, a quantity, and an opinion do not answer a price question.

items.stem: You hear '취미가 뭐예요?' (chwimiga mwoyeyo?) meaning 'What is your hobby?'. Which reply fits?
options: 저는 학생이에요 (jeoneun haksaengieyo) - I am a student
오늘은 추워요 (oneureun chuwoyo) - Today is cold
학교에 가요 (hakgyoe gayo) - I go to school
음악 듣는 것을 좋아해요 (eumak deutneun geoseul joahaeyo) - I like listening to music
items.explanation: 취미가 뭐예요? asks about a hobby, so 음악 듣는 것 describes a pastime. Occupation, weather, and a destination answer other questions.

items.stem: You hear '국적이 어디예요?' (gukjeogi eodiyeyo?) meaning 'What is your nationality?'. Which reply is correct?
options: 저는 한국 사람이에요 (jeoneun hanguk saramieyo) - I am Korean
저는 스무 살이에요 (jeoneun seumu sarieyo) - I am twenty
제 이름은 민수예요 (je ireumeun Minsuyeyo) - My name is Minsu
저는 의사예요 (jeoneun uisayeyo) - I am a doctor
items.explanation: 국적 asks nationality, so 저는 한국 사람이에요 states a nationality. Age, name, and occupation answer different personal-information questions.

items.stem: You hear '날씨가 어때요?' (nalssiga eottaeyo?) meaning 'How is the weather?'. Which reply describes it?
options: 오늘은 월요일이에요 (oneureun woryoilieyo) - Today is Monday
오늘은 추워요 (oneureun chuwoyo) - Today it is cold
날씨를 좋아해요 (nalssireul joahaeyo) - I like the weather
네, 맞아요 (ne, majayo) - Yes, that is right
items.explanation: 날씨가 어때요? asks for a weather description, so 오늘은 추워요 says it is cold. A weekday, a preference, and agreement do not describe the weather.

items.stem: You hear a short exchange at a store: '가게에서 뭘 사요?' - '빵을 사요.' (What do you buy at the store? - I buy bread.) What is the main topic?
items.explanation: The speakers discuss buying 빵 'bread', so the topic is shopping. Travel, exercise, and weather are not mentioned in the dialogue.

items.stem: You hear: '어제 뭐 했어요?' - '친구하고 영화를 봤어요.' (What did you do yesterday? - I watched a movie with a friend.) What is the topic?
items.explanation: The answer describes watching a movie with a friend, which is a leisure activity. Occupation, food, and transportation are not discussed in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear at a restaurant: '뭘 드릴까요?' - '비빔밥 하나 주세요.' (What may I bring you? - One bibimbap, please.) What is happening?
options: 길을 물어봐요 (gireul mureobwayo) - asking for directions
값을 깎아요 (gapseul kkakayo) - bargaining over price
items.explanation: The customer orders 비빔밥, so 음식을 주문해요 'ordering food' fits. There is no request for directions, bargaining, or greeting in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear: '지금 어디예요?' - '저는 도서관에 있어요.' (Where are you now? - I am at the library.) Where is the speaker?
items.explanation: The speaker says 도서관에 있어요, which means 'I am at the library'. The other places are not mentioned in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear: '몇 살이에요?' - '스무 살이에요.' (How old are you? - I am twenty.) Which information did the answer give?
items.explanation: The answer 스무 살 gives an age, so the question asked about 나이. Address, phone number, and occupation are different personal details.

items.stem: You hear: '가방 안에 뭐가 있어요?' - '책과 공책이 있어요.' (What is in the bag? - There are a book and a notebook.) What is in the bag?
options: 사과와 우유 (sagwa wa uyu) - an apple and milk
옷과 신발 (otgwa sinbal) - clothes and shoes
돈과 열쇠 (dongwa yeolsoe) - money and keys
책과 공책 (chaekgwa gongchaek) - a book and a notebook
items.explanation: The speaker lists 책과 공책 'a book and a notebook', so that is the correct content. The other pairs are not mentioned in the dialogue.

items.stem: You hear: '오늘 날씨가 어때요?' - '비가 와요.' (How is the weather today? - It is raining.) What is the weather like?
items.explanation: The speaker says 비가 와요 'it is raining', so rain is the weather. Snow, wind, and clouds are not stated in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear: '주말에 뭐 해요?' - '수영을 해요.' (What do you do on weekends? - I swim.) Which activity is mentioned?
items.explanation: The answer 수영을 해요 means 'I swim', so swimming is the activity. Hiking, reading, and fishing are not mentioned in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear: '어떻게 가요?' - '버스를 타요.' (How do you go? - I take the bus.) Which transportation is used?
items.explanation: The speaker says 버스를 타요 'I take the bus', so bus is the means of transport. Subway, taxi, and train are not mentioned.

items.stem: You hear: '생일 파티에 와요?' - '네, 갈게요.' (Will you come to the birthday party? - Yes, I will go.) What event is mentioned?
options: 운동 경기 (undong gyeonggi) - a sports game
생일 파티 (saengil pati) - a birthday party
items.explanation: The dialogue mentions 생일 파티 'birthday party', so that is the event. A wedding, a meeting, and a sports game are not mentioned.

items.stem: You hear: '여기서 커피를 마셔요?' - '아니요, 가지고 가요.' (Are you drinking coffee here? - No, I take it out.) Where will the coffee be drunk?
items.explanation: The reply 가지고 가요 means 'to take it away', so the coffee is drunk outside the shop. 'At the shop' and 'here' contradict the answer, and 'home' is not stated.

items.stem: You hear: '시간이 있어요?' - '미안해요, 지금 바빠요.' (Do you have time? - Sorry, I am busy now.) How does the speaker respond?
items.explanation: The speaker says 미안해요, 지금 바빠요 'Sorry, I am busy', which declines the request. Agreeing, gladness, and thanks do not match the reply.

items.stem: You hear: '무슨 색을 좋아해요?' - '파란색을 좋아해요.' (What color do you like? - I like blue.) Which color is liked?
items.explanation: The speaker says 파란색을 좋아해요 'I like blue', so blue is correct. Red, yellow, and black are not mentioned in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear: '학교에서 집까지 얼마나 걸려요?' - '삼십 분 걸려요.' (How long from school to home? - It takes thirty minutes.) How long does it take?
items.explanation: The speaker says 삼십 분 걸려요 'it takes thirty minutes', so thirty minutes is correct. The other durations are not stated.

items.stem: You hear: '저 사람은 누구예요?' - '제 선생님이에요.' (Who is that person? - That is my teacher.) Who is the person?
items.explanation: The speaker says 제 선생님이에요 'that is my teacher', so the person is a teacher. Doctor, friend, and family are not mentioned in the exchange.

items.stem: You hear: '뭘 마실래요?' - '주스를 마실래요.' (What would you like to drink? - I would like juice.) What will the speaker drink?
items.explanation: The speaker says 주스를 마실래요 'I would like juice', so juice is the drink. Milk, tea, and water are not mentioned in the exchange.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'apple' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: The word 사과 means 'apple'. 포도, 바나나, and 딸기 mean grape, banana, and strawberry respectively, so they are incorrect.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'water' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: The basic Korean word for water is 물. 우유, 주스, and 차 mean milk, juice, and tea, which are different drinks.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'school' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: 학교 means 'school'. 병원, 식당, and 회사 mean hospital, restaurant, and company, which are different places.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'friend' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: 친구 means 'friend'. 가족, 선생님, and 이웃 mean family, teacher, and neighbour, so they do not match the meaning.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'bag' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: 가방 means 'bag'. 모자, 신발, and 안경 mean hat, shoes, and glasses, which are different personal items.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'book' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: 책 means 'book'. 공책, 신문, and 잡지 mean notebook, newspaper, and magazine, which are different reading materials.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'chair' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: 의자 means 'chair'. 책상, 침대, and 문 mean desk, bed, and door, which are different objects or furniture.

items.stem: Which Korean word means 'meat' in a beginner vocabulary list?
items.explanation: 고기 means 'meat'. 생선, 야채, and 과일 mean fish, vegetables, and fruit, which are different food types.

items.stem: Choose the correct particle: 저__ 학생이에요. (jeo__ haksaengieyo) 'I am a student.'
items.explanation: The topic particle 는 marks 저 'I' as the topic, giving 저는 학생이에요. 를 is an object particle, 에 marks time or place, and 와 means 'and', so none of them fit.

items.stem: Choose the correct particle: 밥__ 먹어요. (bap__ meogeoyo) 'I eat rice.'
items.explanation: 밥 ends in a consonant, so the object particle 을 is used, giving 밥을 먹어요. 은 is a topic particle, 에 marks time or place, and 도 means 'also'.

items.stem: Choose the correct particle: 학교__ 가요. (hakgyo__ gayo) 'I go to school.'
items.explanation: The particle 에 marks a destination, giving 학교에 가요 'I go to school'. 를 is an object particle, 은 is a topic particle, and 와 means 'and'.

items.stem: Choose the correct particle: 책이 책상 위__ 있어요. (chaegi chaeksang wi__ isseoyo) 'The book is on the desk.'
items.explanation: The particle 에 marks location together with 있어요, giving 책상 위에 있어요 'on the desk'. 를 is an object particle, 는 is a topic particle, and 과 means 'and'.

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form: 내일 친구를 ___. (naeil chingureul ___) 'I will meet a friend tomorrow.'
options: 만날 수 없어요 (mannal su eopseoyo) - cannot meet
만나지 마세요 (mannaji maseyo) - do not meet
items.explanation: With the future time word 내일, the present-tense form 만나요 expresses a planned future action. 만났어요 is past, while the other two express inability or prohibition.

items.stem: Choose the correct verb form: 어제 영화를 ___. (eoje yeonghwareul ___) 'I watched a movie yesterday.'
options: 보지 마세요 (boji maseyo) - do not watch
items.explanation: The past time word 어제 requires the past tense 봤어요 'watched'. 봐요 is present, 볼 거예요 is future, and 보지 마세요 is a prohibition.

items.stem: Choose the correct form: 물을 ___. (mureul ___) 'I want to drink water.'
options: 마시고 싶어요 (masigo sipeoyo) - want to drink
마시면 안 돼요 (masimyeon an dwaeyo) - must not drink
마시기 싫어요 (masigi sileoyo) - do not want to drink
items.explanation: The pattern -고 싶어요 expresses 'want to', giving 마시고 싶어요 'want to drink'. The plain present and the forms meaning 'must not drink' and 'do not want to drink' do not match.

items.stem: Choose the correct negative form: 밥을 ___. (babeul ___) 'I do not eat rice.'
options: 안 먹어요 (an meogeoyo) - do not eat
items.explanation: The short negative 안 before a verb gives 안 먹어요 'do not eat'. The other options are the positive present, past, and future forms, so they are not negative.

items.stem: Which sentence correctly uses the past tense to say 'I met a friend yesterday.'?
options: 어제 친구를 만날 거예요 (eoje chingureul mannal geoyeyo)
어제 친구를 만나고 싶어요 (eoje chingureul mannago sipeoyo)
items.explanation: 어제 'yesterday' requires the past tense, so 만났어요 is correct. 만나요 is present, 만날 거예요 is future, and 만나고 싶어요 means 'want to meet'.

items.stem: Read: '저는 매일 아침 여섯 시에 일어나요. 그리고 학교에 가요.' (I get up at six every morning and then go to school.) When does the writer get up?
items.explanation: The passage says 여섯 시에 일어나요 'I get up at six o'clock', so six o'clock is correct. The other times are not stated in the passage.

items.stem: Read: '오늘은 날씨가 좋아요. 하늘이 맑아요.' (The weather is nice today; the sky is clear.) How is the weather today?
items.explanation: The passage says 하늘이 맑아요 'the sky is clear', so clear is correct. Cloudy, rainy, and snowy do not match the stated weather.

items.stem: Read: '저는 시장에서 사과와 우유를 샀어요.' (I bought apples and milk at the market.) What did the writer buy?
options: 빵과 물 (ppangwa mul) - bread and water
사과와 우유 (sagwa wa uyu) - apples and milk
고기와 밥 (gogigwa bap) - meat and rice
과일과 차 (gwailgwa cha) - fruit and tea
items.explanation: The passage states 사과와 우유를 샀어요 'bought apples and milk', so that pair is correct. The other pairs are not mentioned in the passage.

items.stem: Read: '우리 가족은 네 명이에요. 아버지, 어머니, 누나 그리고 저예요.' (My family has four people: father, mother, older sister, and me.) How many people are in the family?
items.explanation: The passage says 우리 가족은 네 명이에요 'my family has four people', so four is correct. The other numbers do not match the stated count.

items.stem: Read: '제 취미는 사진을 찍는 것이에요. 주말에 사진을 찍어요.' (My hobby is taking photos; I take photos on weekends.) What is the writer's hobby?
items.explanation: The passage says 취미는 사진을 찍는 것이에요 'my hobby is taking photos', so that is correct. The other hobbies are not stated in the passage.

items.stem: Read: '동생은 대학생이에요. 서울에서 공부해요.' (My younger sibling is a university student and studies in Seoul.) Who is the university student?
items.explanation: The passage says 동생은 대학생이에요 'my younger sibling is a university student', so 동생 is correct. The writer, mother, and friend are not described as students.

items.stem: Choose the best reply: '가: 만나서 반가워요. 나: ___.' (A: Nice to meet you. B: ___)
options: 안녕히 계세요 (annyeonghi gyeseyo) - Goodbye to one staying
저도 반가워요 (jeodo bangawoyo) - Nice to meet you too
잘 먹겠습니다 (jal meokgetseumnida) - I will eat well
items.explanation: 만나서 반가워요 'nice to meet you' is answered with 저도 반가워요 'nice to meet you too'. Goodbye, happy birthday, and the mealtime phrase do not fit the greeting.

items.stem: Choose the best reply: '가: 감사합니다. 나: ___.' (A: Thank you. B: ___)
items.explanation: Thanking is answered with 천만에요 'you're welcome'. A greeting, 'excuse me', and an apology do not reply to thanks in Korean.

items.stem: Read: '저는 아침에 빵을 먹어요. 점심에는 밥을 먹어요. 저녁에는 국수를 먹어요.' (I eat bread in the morning, rice at lunch, and noodles in the evening.) What is the main idea?
options: 여행 계획 (yeohaeng gyehoek) - a travel plan
하루 세 끼 식사 (haru se kki siksa) - the day's three meals
items.explanation: The passage lists what the writer eats for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, so the main idea is the day's meals. Travel, exercise, and school are not discussed.

items.stem: Read: '주말에 저는 등산을 좋아해요. 산에 가면 기분이 좋아요.' (On weekends I like hiking; when I go to the mountains I feel good.) What is the main idea?
options: 주말 취미로 등산 (jumal chwimi ro deungsan) - hiking as a weekend hobby
여행 준비 (yeohaeng junbi) - preparing for a trip
items.explanation: The passage says the writer likes hiking on weekends and feels good in the mountains, so hiking as a weekend hobby is the main idea. Travel, morning exercise, and reading are not discussed.

items.stem: Read the sign: '도서관은 아홉 시에 열어요. 일요일에는 쉬어요.' (The library opens at nine and is closed on Sundays.) When is the library closed?
items.explanation: The sign says 일요일에는 쉬어요 'closed on Sundays', so Sunday is correct. Monday, Saturday, and Friday are not stated as closing days on the sign.

items.stem: Read: '수업은 아홉 시에 시작해요. 그리고 열두 시에 끝나요.' (Class starts at nine and ends at twelve.) When does class end?
items.explanation: The passage says 열두 시에 끝나요 'it ends at twelve', so twelve is correct. Nine is the start time, and the other times are not stated.

items.stem: Read: '토요일 오후 두 시에 생일 파티가 있어요. 우리 집에서 만나요.' (There is a birthday party at two on Saturday afternoon; we meet at my house.) Where is the party held?
items.explanation: The invitation says 우리 집에서 만나요 'we meet at my house', so the party is at the house. Restaurant, park, and school are not mentioned.
